# One row per PROMISE claim of the live claims document: kind PROMISE, or a STATE or MIXED claim whose
# UNMEASURED reason is PROMISE. Built from the code, the workflows and the pages at commit 778d653 and read
# against the White Paper (docs/GNI_WHITE_PAPER_S107.md). Check C20 (`promise ledger`) holds it.
# R11 (S112): the founding philosophy's 28 rules (docs/GNI_PHILOSOPHY_S112.md, CLM-1106..CLM-1133) are
# graded too, and CLM-092's note is corrected (R10 said the historical context was fed to the analysis;
# it is attached to the report after the analysis).
# R12 (S112): CLM-1132 corrected to BUILT (the cross-run verdict history R11's search missed); CLM-1116
# re-graded after DECISION S112-6 turned off the quality-score -> source-weight channel; CLM-1127 and
# CLM-1131 record the operator's S34 shelving of adversarial feeds.
# S113 R1: the five errors S112 found in its own grading after it shipped are corrected
# re-graded PARTIAL; the notes of CLM-1111, CLM-1125 and CLM-1127 say what the code holds; the
# ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 citation, read from its abstract only, is dropped (R-S112-2).
#   BUILT      what the sentence promises runs, or holds, in the tree today (a standing commitment - the
#              disclaimer, free access - is BUILT while it holds). Where the build differs in a detail
#              from the sentence (four agents, not three), the note says how.
#   PARTIAL    part of it runs; the note names what does not.
#   NOT BUILT  nothing in the tree does it. A promise dated in the future is NOT BUILT, with its due
#              date in the note; a past due date is said in the note too.
#   WITHDRAWN  only by a DECISION of the operator's, cited as DECISION:S<n>-<k> and recorded in the
#              live order. A session grades a promise; it does not retire one GNI made.
# EVIDENCE   space-separated: a repo path (must exist), a claim id of the tree (CLM-###), or for
#            WITHDRAWN a DECISION token. The note says what was read and what was found, so each
#            grade can be checked against its evidence by a person.
# GRADING IS A PERSON'S JUDGEMENT, made by Claude at S112 from the files named; roadmap 4's Test 2
# is the operator's verdict on it. Guidelines: ISO/IEC/IEEE 15026-2:2022 (an assurance case: claims
# with argument and evidence) - only its published scope is relied on here, no clause is cited.
